_doc: Kill-count floors per (suite::module). Tier is assigned by measured suite runtime -- see tools/mutation_ratchet.py. min_kill/module_hash/measured_at are written by --baseline and must never be hand-edited: a floor typed from memory measures memory.

tools/test_egcc_residue.py::modules/rule._why_weekly: each rule_compiler pair costs about 22s (test_egcc_residue.py runs 3.2s x 7 runs). Both on push measured 95.7s for the tier; schema.py is the core surface and stays, parser.py moves here.

tools/test_architectural_truth.py::modul._why: LAW II grader. Enrolled after its first probe returned PARTIAL (5/6, frozen=True survived): the suite reported 14/14 while nothing pinned the canonical pairs as immutable.

tools/test_done_strength_ladder.py::modu._why: LAW IX grader. Enrolled after its first probe returned PARTIAL (4/6): the suite reported 13/13 while the unknown-list assertion only checked non-emptiness and the fail-closed rung was unpinned.

tools/test_foreign_hunk_guard.py::tools/._why: Same-file concurrent-writer guard. Enrolled after its first probe returned PARTIAL (3/6): a flipped success exit code kept all five exit codes distinct and survived, and a check=False inside the VERIFY_MISMATCH branch survived because nothing had ever driven the guard's most important refusal -- the honest 'I cannot tell your lines from theirs'. Only tier and this note are hand-written; the floor is measured by --baseline.

tools/test_duplicate_to_advantage.py::mo._why_weekly: the suite runs 35.2s, so a 4-mutant sweep costs about 3 minutes -- roughly ten times the whole push tier. Move to "push" if that cost is acceptable.
